stemMd:
At point **[2]** in paragraph 3, the writer is considering adding the following sentence:

> The library also runs a monthly book club that meets in the same room as the seed cabinet.

Should the writer make this addition?

options.label: A
options.textMd: No, because the book club was already described in paragraph 2, alongside the borrowing rules.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Yes, because it tells the reader which room of the library the seed cabinet is kept in.

options.label: C
options.textMd: No, because it does nothing to develop the paragraph’s point about what the collection records.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Yes, because it shows that the library serves Cedar Hollow in more ways than simply lending seed.

explanationMd:
Work out what the paragraph is doing before you judge the sentence. Paragraph 3 makes one point: the borrowing record has become evidence of a changing climate. Every sentence in it supports that point — beans finishing earlier, okra becoming the most borrowed packet, the extension office citing the ledger.

A book club is a true and pleasant fact about the library, but it says nothing about what the collection records, so it interrupts the paragraph’s line of thought. The addition should be rejected.

Check your answer by reading the paragraph with the sentence inserted: if you cannot say what the new sentence adds to the paragraph’s argument, it does not belong. Note also that a choice can give a true reason and still be wrong — the question is not "is this interesting?" but "does this serve the paragraph?"

distractorRationale.d: Accepts the sentence because the information is agreeable and true. Relevance on the ACT is judged against the purpose of the specific paragraph, not against the passage’s general subject; showing that the Cedar Hollow library does more than lend seed is not what paragraph 3 is doing.
distractorRationale.b: Treats an incidental clause ("in the same room as the seed cabinet") as though location were the point, and overstates it besides: the sentence never names the room. The paragraph is about what the ledger data show, and the reader has no need of the cabinet’s location at this point.
distractorRationale.a: Rejects the sentence for a reason that is factually false: paragraph 2 covers only the borrowing rules and the ledger, and the book club is never mentioned anywhere else in the passage. Always verify a claim about what the passage already says before choosing an answer that rests on it.

accessibilityText: The question asks whether to add the sentence "The library also runs a monthly book club that meets in the same room as the seed cabinet" to the third paragraph, which is about what the seed-borrowing records show about the local climate.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Paragraph 3 is about the collection as a climate record and the ledger totals sent to the extension office; a sentence about a book club meeting in the seed-cabinet room contributes nothing to that point. The book club is never mentioned in paragraph 2 (so the 'already described' option is factually false), the sentence does not actually name the room, and 'serves the town in more ways' is off the paragraph's focus. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-cue-batch1-run1) reached the same answer: Paragraph 3 is about the collection as a climate record (beans finishing early, okra now most borrowed, ledger totals sent to the extension office). A book-club sentence is off that point, so 'No, it does not develop the point about what the collection records' is right. The 'already described in paragraph 2' option is factually false (paragraph 2 never mentions a book club); the 'tells which room' option misstates what the sentence does and is irrelevant anyway; the 'serves the town in more ways' option names a point the paragraph is not making.]
